source: NCERT Class VII, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 1.

sections.heading: 1. Science as a Way of Knowing
points: **Science** is an ever-evolving body of knowledge built by **observation, questioning, experiment and reasoning**.
Scientific ideas can **change** as new evidence appears — science is **self-correcting**.
Curiosity and careful observation drive every discovery.

sections.heading: 2. The Scientific Method
points: **Observe → Question → Hypothesis (guess) → Experiment → Record & Analyse → Conclude → Test again.**
A **hypothesis** is a testable explanation; an **experiment** must be **fair** (change one factor at a time).
Science relies on **evidence and measurement**, not opinion.

sections.heading: 3. Science, Technology and Society
points: **Science** = knowledge of nature; **technology** = applying it to make useful tools.
Science and technology have transformed **health, food, communication and transport**.
Indian contributions: e.g. **Aryabhata** (astronomy/maths), **C. V. Raman** (Raman Effect), **ISRO** (space).

sections.heading: 4. Doing Science Responsibly
points: Scientists must be **honest, careful and open** to being proved wrong.
Science should be used for the **good of society and the environment**.
Anyone who observes, questions and tests carefully can 'think like a scientist'.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Science = observation + questioning + experiment + reasoning; self-correcting.
Method: observe → question → hypothesis → experiment → analyse → conclude.
Fair test = change one factor at a time.
Science = knowledge; technology = its application.
C. V. Raman = Raman Effect; ISRO = India's space agency.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: Scientific knowledge can **change** with new evidence — it is not fixed.
A **fair test** changes only **one variable** at a time.
**Science** (knowledge) and **technology** (application) are related but distinct.
A **hypothesis** must be **testable**.
